blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Managing tax risk and penalties at scale is, in the end, the disciplined work of keeping small incidents small. Every large group has issues — a misclassification somewhere, a late filing in a minor entity, a borderline position that an auditor happens to disagree with. None of these, caught early and handled cleanly, grows into a material problem. Several of them, left to accumulate quietly, can combine into a very uncomfortable narrative at the next audit.

The senior discipline is triage. Every issue, the moment it surfaces, is classified by size, documented, and given an owner. Small issues are resolved and closed. Medium issues are tracked quarterly. Large issues go directly to the executive committee. Nothing is left to drift.

Had we not resolved the three small penalties last year, they would have become the case study our competitors are now reading about. That sentence is the quiet motto of senior tax risk leadership — which is, when you strip away the drama, a discipline of patient, unglamorous triage.

items.q: According to the text, what determines whether small issues become a material problem?
options: Whether the auditor is experienced
Whether they are caught early and handled cleanly
How many jurisdictions the group operates in
The size of the penalty involved
items.why: "None of these, caught early and handled cleanly, grows into a material problem."

items.q: How are large issues handled under the triage system described?
options: They are resolved and closed at the operational level
They are left to accumulate until the next audit
They are tracked quarterly
They go directly to the executive committee
items.why: "Large issues go directly to the executive committee."

items.q: What does the phrase "a very uncomfortable narrative at the next audit" most likely refer to?
options: A single catastrophic error discovered by chance
The combined effect of several small issues left unaddressed
A change in tax legislation
A disagreement between two auditors
items.why: Inferência: o texto liga a narrativa a vários problemas pequenos que se acumulam em silêncio.

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: Penalty management should be systematic rather than ad hoc
Small tax incidents are inevitable in any large group
Documenting and assigning ownership reduces exposure
Waiting to see if minor issues resolve themselves is prudent
items.why: Inferência: o texto inteiro defende agir cedo — deixar problemas 'à deriva' é justamente o que ele condena.

items.q: What does the closing description "patient, unglamorous triage" suggest about the work?
options: It can be delegated to junior staff entirely
It is dramatic and high-profile by nature
It is largely a matter of legal expertise
It is undervalued but quietly decisive
items.why: Inferência: 'unglamorous' e 'quiet motto' indicam trabalho discreto, sem holofote, mas que decide o resultado.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Charlotte fechando três casos de penalidade antes que se combinem com qualquer outra coisa. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Right, three cases and I want all of them closed before quarter end. None of them is large on its own — a late filing in the Rotterdam entity, a misclassified charge, and a borderline position the auditor flagged but hasn't pressed. Individually, trivial. Together, at next year's audit, they'd read like a pattern. And a pattern is what turns a small penalty into a headline.

So, the discipline is simple, if you actually do it. Each one gets classified by size, documented properly, and given a single owner. Not a committee — an owner. The Rotterdam filing I'm closing myself this week. The misclassification goes to Daniel, who booked it, with a note on the correct treatment. The borderline position we document fully and hold, because that one I want on record either way.

Had we let last year's three small penalties sit, they'd be the case study our competitors are circulating right now. We didn't, so they aren't. That's the whole job, honestly. It's unglamorous, nobody thanks you for it, and it's precisely why nothing lands on the executive committee's desk that shouldn't be there.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: Why does Charlotte want the three cases closed before quarter end?
options: The auditor has already pressed the borderline position
The executive committee has demanded it
Each one is individually severe
Together they could read like a pattern at next year's audit
items.why: "Together, at next year's audit, they'd read like a pattern."

items.q: How is Charlotte handling the misclassified charge?
options: She is escalating it to the executive committee
She is holding it fully documented for the record
She is closing it herself this week
She is assigning it to Daniel, who booked it, with a note on treatment
items.why: "The misclassification goes to Daniel, who booked it, with a note on the correct treatment."

items.q: Why does Charlotte insist on "an owner. Not a committee"?
options: A single owner ensures clear accountability for closing the issue
The committee is already overloaded
Ownership is required by Dutch law
Committees are cheaper to run
items.why: Inferência: um dono único responde pelo fechamento — um comitê dilui a responsabilidade.

items.q: What does Charlotte imply about the value of this work?
options: It is glamorous and widely recognised
It should be automated to save effort
It is thankless but prevents bigger problems from reaching the top
It is mostly a legal formality
items.why: Inferência: 'unglamorous, nobody thanks you' + 'nothing lands on the committee's desk that shouldn't be there'.

items.q: Why is Charlotte documenting the borderline position rather than closing it?
options: Because she wants it on record regardless of how it goes
Because Daniel booked it incorrectly
Because it is the largest of the three cases
Because the auditor has already rejected it
items.why: "we document fully and hold, because that one I want on record either way."

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Left unchecked, the exposure could turn into a material problem for the group." A material problem is one that…
options: only affects a single minor entity
concerns physical assets rather than tax
is significant enough to affect the financial picture
has already been fully documented
items.why: Material problem = problema material, relevante o bastante para pesar no resultado.

items.q: "The desk took a borderline position that the auditor could reasonably challenge." This is a position that is…
options: at the edge of what the rules allow, open to disagreement
already rejected by the tax authority
clearly compliant and beyond dispute
purely internal and never disclosed
items.why: Borderline position = posição limítrofe, no limite do defensável.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Small issues that are left to ___ quietly can combine into something serious."
options: accumulate
document
resolve
classify
items.why: To accumulate = acumular-se; é o verbo que descreve problemas somando-se em silêncio.

items.q: "The senior discipline is triage." In this context, triage means…
options: documenting issues without acting on them
outsourcing risk assessment to auditors
escalating every issue to the executive committee
sorting issues by size and priority so each is handled appropriately
items.why: Triage = triagem: classificar por gravidade/prioridade para tratar cada caso do jeito certo.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "Every exposure must be assessed and reported to the ___, which owns the largest risks."
options: material problem
institutional memory
executive committee
borderline position
items.why: Executive committee = comitê executivo, para onde vão os riscos grandes.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem em reuniões de gestão de risco tributário. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The committee still has to sign off on the provision before we book it." To sign off on means to…
options: quietly ignore
delegate downward
reopen for debate
formally approve
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "Two entities pushed back on the reclassification." They…
options: approved it immediately
documented it in full
escalated it to the auditor
resisted or disagreed with it
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar, sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "We agreed the mitigation plan, but nobody followed through." They…
options: carried it out to completion
failed to carry it to completion
reported it to the committee
rewrote it from scratch
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado — aqui, não aconteceu.

items.q: "Closing three minor penalties won't move the needle on the group's overall exposure." This means it will…
options: create serious resistance
not make a noticeable difference
make a decisive difference
take years to measure
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível; com 'won't', não muda nada relevante.

items.q: "Let's get ahead of the audit and document the borderline positions now." To get ahead of something means to…
options: hand it over to a competitor
overstate its importance to the board
postpone it until absolutely necessary
deal with it proactively before it becomes a problem
items.why: Get ahead of = antecipar-se, agir antes que o problema cresça — o próprio espírito da triagem da lição.
